title: Development of a pyrosequencing assay for the typing of alphaherpesviruses☆
author: Fusco, Amoroso, et al.
materials: Reference strains of BoHV-1.1, BoHV-1.2, BoHV-5 and CpHV-1 were supplied by Dr. M. Beer from FLI (Friedrich Loeffler Institut, Germany). Bubaline herpesvirus 1 (strain Metzler) was kindly provided by Prof. U. Pagnini (University of Naples Federico II, Italy).•3–7 mm stainless steel beads•Disposable scalpel•Sterile pincers and scissors•QIAamp viral RNA mini kit (Qiagen)•Technical scale•Tissue Lyser (Qiagen)

•Prepare, in a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube, the immobilization solution by mixing (per sample): 2 μl steptavidin-coated Sepharose beads together with 40 μl Binding buffer and 18 μl high-purity water.•Transfer biotinylated amplified samples (20 μl) to the wells of a PCR plate.•Add 60 μl of immobilization solution to the samples in the PCR plate.•Seal the plate and capture PCR products on the steptavidin-coated beads by shaking the plate on a plate mixer for 10 min at 1400 rpm.•In the meanwhile prepare the vacuum workstation by filling the 5 troughs with the following solutions:1)50 ml ethanol 70%2)40 ml Denaturation solution3)50 ml 1x Washing buffer4)50 ml high-purity water5)70 ml high-purity water•Immediately after immobilization perform separation of biotinylated PCR strands from non-biotinylated strands in the vacuum workstation as indicated in the PyroMark user manual. Note: Beads sediment quickly, so be careful to perform this step right away after the capture.•At the end of the procedure samples will be realized into a PyroMArk Q24 (PMQ) plate which contains 25 μl (per well) of the sequencing primer (opportunely diluted to 0.3 μM in the Annealing buffer).•Accommodate the PMQ plate into the PyroMark Plate Holder•Perform annealing of the primer to the samples by heating the PyroMark plate at 80 °C for 2 min and cooling it for 5 min at room temperature.•Prepare the Gold Q24 reagents (enzyme and substrate mixtures) as indicated by the manufacturer.•Select the PRP in the PyroMark Q24 2.0.6 software and set the number of samples and the scheme of the PMQ plate.•Transfer, with the help of the electronic key, the assay information on the PyroMark Q24 station.•Pipet the PRP established amount of reagents into the cartridge compartments according to Fig. 3.•Place the PMQ plate and the cartridge in the instrument and start the run.•Analyze obtained pyrograms (Fig. 4) with the PMQ24 sequencing software (Qiagen).•Classify the herpesvirus comparing the sequence obtained to those expected for each strain. Note: The lists of materials include only non standard items. General materials like microcentrifuge tubes, or PBS are assumed to be available. For PCR and pyrosequencing steps it is recommended to use only PCR clean disposable items.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue sample
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:10 tissue‑to‑PBS suspension and homogenize until no visible debris remains.

substeps.instruction: Cut the tissue into small pieces with a scalpel, sterile pincers and scissors.
Weigh 150 mg of tissue and place it in a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add one stainless‑steel bead (3–7 mm diameter) and 1.5 ml PBS (maintaining the 1:10 ratio; adjust volume if tissue amount changes).
Homogenize in a TissueLyser for 5 min at 30 Hz (extend the time if debris is still visible).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Separate the homogenate by centrifugation and transfer the clarified supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 15 min at 4000 × g, 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Extract nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Purify viral nucleic acids from the supernatant using the QIAamp Viral RNA Mini Kit.

substeps.instruction: Process 140 µl of the supernatant according to the kit handbook.
Elute nucleic acids in 50 µl QIAamp elution buffer.

steps.title: Store or use DNA
steps.instruction: Proceed directly to PCR or store the extracted DNA at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Assemble the PCR reaction mixture for each sample.

substeps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml tube combine per sample: 12.5 µl PyroMark PCR master mix, 1.25 µl forward primer (0.2 µM), 1.25 µl reverse primer (0.2 µM, biotinylated), and 5 µl Qsolution (total 20 µl).
Dispense 20 µl of the mix into a 0.2 ml PCR tube.
Add 5 µl of the extracted DNA to the tube.

steps.title: Run PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the target region with the following thermal profile and verify the product.

substeps.instruction: 95 °C for 15 min (initial activation).
45 cycles of: 94 °C for 30 s, 60 °C for 30 s, 72 °C for 30 s.
72 °C for 10 min (final elongation).
Check the PCR product by capillary electrophoresis (or agarose gel if capillary system unavailable).

steps.title: Immobilize biotinylated PCR
steps.instruction: Capture biotin‑labeled amplicons on streptavidin‑coated beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare immobilization solution per sample: 2 µl streptavidin‑coated Sepharose beads, 40 µl Binding buffer, 18 µl high‑purity water.
Transfer 20 µl of the biotinylated PCR to wells of a PCR plate.
Add 60 µl immobilization solution to each well, seal the plate, and shake for 10 min at 1400 rpm.

steps.title: Set up vacuum workstation
steps.instruction: Load the vacuum workstation with the required reagents for strand separation.

substeps.instruction: Trough 1: 50 ml 70 % ethanol.
Trough 2: 40 ml Denaturation solution.
Trough 3: 50 ml 1× Washing buffer.
Trough 4: 50 ml high‑purity water.
Trough 5: 70 ml high‑purity water.

steps.title: Separate DNA strands
steps.instruction: Immediately after immobilization, separate biotinylated strands from non‑biotinylated strands using the vacuum workstation as described in the PyroMark user manual.

steps.title: Add sequencing primer
steps.instruction: Dispense sequencing primer into the PyroMark Q24 (PMQ) plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 µl per well of sequencing primer (0.3 µM in Annealing buffer).
Place the PMQ plate into the PyroMark Plate Holder.

steps.title: Anneal primer to template
steps.instruction: Hybridize the sequencing primer to the captured DNA.

substeps.instruction: Heat the plate at 80 °C for 2 min.
Cool at room temperature for 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare Q24 reagents
steps.instruction: Make the Gold Q24 enzyme and substrate mixtures according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Load software and reagents
steps.instruction: Configure the PyroMark Q24 instrument and load the reaction cartridge.

substeps.instruction: In PyroMark Q24 2.0.6 software select PRP, set the number of samples and plate scheme.
Transfer assay information to the instrument using the electronic key.
Pipet the prescribed volumes of reagents into the cartridge compartments as shown in Fig. 3.

steps.title: Run pyrosequencing
steps.instruction: Insert the PMQ plate and cartridge into the PyroMark Q24 and start the run.

steps.title: Analyze pyrograms
steps.instruction: Interpret the sequencing results and assign the herpesvirus strain.

substeps.instruction: Analyze pyrograms with the PMQ24 sequencing software.
Compare the obtained sequence to reference strain sequences to classify the virus.

description: In short the typing of the alphaherpesviruses by pyrosequencing is made as follows: (A) extraction of DNA from the samples; (B) PCR amplification with two amplification primers (forward and reverse) that are specific to the sequence of interest, one of which (in our case the reverse primer) is biotinylated; (C) capture of biotin-labeled single-stranded PCR products (ssDNA) and separation from non biotin-labeled strands; (D) incubation of the ssDNA with the sequencing primer; (E) sequencing of the variable region by pyrosequencing; (F) analysis of the pyrograms obtained and classification of the strain of herpesvirus.
